findings.issue_text: tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py:3624 — The commit that changes `upsampled_count`'s `default_result_type` from `"integer"` to `"number"` (src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1051) simultaneously deletes the `meta["fields"]["count"] == "integer"` assertion in `test_error_upsampling_basic_functionality` instead of updating it to assert `"number"` — this is a textbook silent-pass pattern: the test no longer proves what type the API actually returns, so a real client-facing type regression (count field switching from integer to float/number for widgets, alerting thresholds, CSV exports) ships with a still-green CI.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py:229 — Removal of `raise ParseError("Cannot group by timestamp")` when `top_events > 0` and grouping by "timestamp" silently changes a previously-400 request into a 200 response with a new response shape (per-timestamp grouping keys), which is an undocumented breaking behavior change for external API callers relying on the old validation/error contract; scope also exceeds the stated "performance optimization" intent.

src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:43 — _are_all_projects_error_upsampled` flips semantics from ANY-project-in-allowlist to ALL-projects-in-allowlist, so multi-project queries with a mixed (partially allowlisted) project set now silently return non-upsampled (lower) `count` values instead of upsampled ones — a response-value contract change with no versioning/deprecation for existing API consumers depending on the prior behavior.

src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1042 — upsampled_eps()` and `upsampled_epm()` SnQLFunctions were removed entirely from DiscoverDatasetConfig; any external API caller previously passing `yAxis=upsampled_eps()`/`upsampled_epm()` will now get a query/validation error where the call previously succeeded — a breaking removal of a public query function.

src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:1051 — default_result_type` for `upsampled_count` changed from "integer" to "number", changing the `meta.fields` type info returned to API clients for that field; the corresponding assertion (`meta["fields"]["count"] == "integer"`) was deleted rather than updated in tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py (around line 3625), masking the type-contract change without establishing/verifying the new correct value.

src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py:77 — transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` no longer converts `sample_count()`/`sample_eps()`/`sample_epm()` back to `count()`/`eps()`/`epm()` (function_conversions dict and convert_fields_for_upsampling were removed), so API consumers that relied on `sample_*` aliased fields to distinguish sampled vs. upsampled responses lose that signal, and `eps()`/`epm()` are no longer transformed for upsampling at all (only `count()` is handled), narrowing previously supported y-axis functions for upsampled queries.

src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py:286 — upsampled_count` now does `sum(Column("sample_weight"))` instead of `sum(ifNull(Column("sample_weight"), 1))`; the docstring's claim that "no additional null checks are needed" is unverified, and if any event in an allowlisted project has a NULL sample_weight (e.g. older events ingested before the column was populated), ClickHouse's `sum()` over a Nullable column will silently exclude those rows (or yield NULL if all rows are NULL), undercounting `count()` for upsampled projects instead of falling back to a weight of 1 as before

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py:204 — use_rpc = dataset in {spans_rpc, ourlogs}` builds a new set literal on every call instead of reusing the previously centralized `RPC_DATASETS` constant; negligible cost but is unnecessary repeated allocation compared to the prior module-level set.

tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py:483 — The removed `meta["fields"]["count"] == "integer"` assertions (previously covering `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects`) were deleted rather than updated to `== "number"`, even though `default_result_type` for `upsampled_count` changed from `"integer"` to `"number"` in src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py, silently dropping coverage for a real API type-contract change.

goldens.comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.
